A straight-on elevation photograph of a multi-story contemporary residential or mixed-use building facade, composed around a concrete structural frame with infill panels of pivoting and sliding perforated screens. The primary facade material is a warm golden-orange perforated metal or terracotta mesh panel system, subdivided into large floor-height bays by the exposed concrete frame. Behind the screens, dark-framed glazed openings are visible at irregular intervals, with some bays open entirely to reveal balcony or terrace spaces. The perforated panel surface has a fine, regular dot pattern that allows diffuse light transmission while providing solar shading and privacy. The color of the panels ranges from bright amber where directly lit to deep orange-brown in shadow. The overall facade composition is characterized by a strict structural grid modulated by the free, operable placement of the screen elements, balancing order and variation across the elevation. The building reads as a contemporary interpretation of a brise-soleil facade system, with the screen panels as the dominant visual element.
